topics.title: Location of Our District in Uganda

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: Name the four cardinal points of a compass.
questions.a: North, East, South and West

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: Name the four semi-cardinal points.
questions.a: North East, South East, South West and North West

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: Give the short form of South West.
questions.a: SW

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: In which direction does the sun rise?
questions.a: In the East

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: In which direction does the sun set?
questions.a: In the West

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: Which way do shadows point in the morning?
questions.a: Towards the west

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: Name the parts of a district, from the biggest to the smallest.
questions.a: District → county or municipality → sub-county or division → parish → village

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: What is a municipality?
questions.a: A large town that has its own council
accepted: A large town that has its own council

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: What is the smallest administrative unit?
questions.a: The village

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: Name any four things found on a good map.
questions.a: Any four of title, key, compass, scale, frame

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: What is the key of a map used for?
questions.a: To explain the symbols used on the map
accepted: To explain the symbols used on the map

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: In what units is the size of a district measured?
questions.a: Square kilometres (km²)

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: Name your own district.
questions.a: (Your own answer — the name of your district.)

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: Name any two districts that border your district.
questions.a: (Your own answer — two districts that touch yours.)

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: Name any three important places found in your district.
questions.a: (Your own answer — for example the district hospital, the main market, a secondary school.)

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: What is a border?
questions.a: The line where two districts meet
accepted: The line where two districts meet

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: Why has Uganda been divided into districts?
questions.a: To bring government services nearer to the people

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: What is a division?
questions.a: A part of a municipality or city (like a sub-county in a town)

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: Give one way of finding direction without a compass.
questions.a: Any one of: use the sun, use shadows, face the sunrise and use your body — East in front, West behind, North on the left, South on the right.
accepted: face the sunrise and use your body — East in front

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: Location of Our District in Uganda
questions.q: Draw the compass showing all eight points.
questions.a: (Your own drawing — it should show N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W and NW in the correct places.)

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What are physical features?
questions.a: Natural things found on the earth's surface that were not made by people.

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any four examples of physical features.
questions.a: Any four of hills, mountains, valleys, plains, rivers, lakes, swamps, forests, rocks, islands

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Which of these is not a physical feature: a lake, a hill, a bridge, a valley?
questions.a: A bridge — it is made by people

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is a river?
questions.a: Water flowing in a channel from a highland to a lake or sea

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is a valley?
questions.a: Low land lying between hills or mountains

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is a plain?
questions.a: Flat or gently sloping land

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any three uses of a lake.
questions.a: Any three of fishing, water for use, transport by boat, tourism, irrigation

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any two uses of a swamp.
questions.a: Any two of papyrus for mats and baskets, clay for bricks and pots, growing rice or yams, home for fish and birds

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any two uses of a forest.
questions.a: Any two of timber, firewood, herbs for medicine, homes for animals, help rainfall

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any two dangers of a river.
questions.a: Any two of drowning, floods, crocodiles and hippos, water-borne diseases such as bilharzia

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give one danger of a steep mountain slope.
questions.a: Landslides (or falling rocks, or soil erosion)

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Which disease do mosquitoes from a swamp spread?
questions.a: Malaria

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any three ways of caring for a lake.
questions.a: Any three of do not throw rubbish in it, do not fish with poison, leave plants on the banks, do not use small nets, do not bathe or wash cars at the source
accepted: do not throw rubbish in it

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is terracing?
questions.a: Cutting steps across a slope to stop soil being washed away

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is soil erosion?
questions.a: The carrying away of soil by water or wind

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is the difference between afforestation and deforestation?
questions.a: Afforestation is planting trees where there were none; deforestation is cutting down trees without replacing them.

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Why do many people settle on plains?
questions.a: Because the land is flat and easy to farm and build on, and there is usually water.

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name one physical feature found in your own district.
questions.a: (Your own answer — a feature really found in your district.)

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give one use of that feature to the people of your district.
questions.a: (Your own answer.)

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give one way the people of your district can care for it.
questions.a: (Your own answer.)

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is vegetation?
questions.a: All the plants growing in a place
accepted: All the plants growing in a place

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name the five types of vegetation given in the syllabus.
questions.a: Forests, swamps, shrubs, grass and crops
accepted: Forests, swamps, shrubs, grass and crops

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is natural vegetation?
questions.a: Vegetation that grew on its own, without being planted by people

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is planted vegetation?
questions.a: Vegetation planted and cared for by people

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give one way of telling a planted forest from a natural forest.
questions.a: A planted forest grows in straight lines and is usually of one kind of tree.

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any four uses of vegetation.
questions.a: Any four of firewood, herbs for medicine, food, oxygen, timber, shade, grazing, beauty, homes for animals, tourism

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Which gas do plants give out that people need?
questions.a: Oxygen

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: How does vegetation help rain to form?
questions.a: Trees give off water vapour, which rises and helps clouds and rain to form.

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: How do the roots of plants help the soil?
questions.a: They hold the soil together so it is not washed or blown away.

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name any four activities of people that destroy vegetation.
questions.a: Any four of burning bushes, over cultivation, over grazing, deforestation, making bricks, road construction, building houses and industries

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is deforestation?
questions.a: Cutting down trees without replacing them
accepted: Cutting down trees without replacing them

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any three results of destroying vegetation.
questions.a: Any three of soil erosion, less rain, drought, wild animals lose homes, shortage of firewood and timber, strong winds, deserts forming

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is afforestation?
questions.a: Planting trees where there were none before

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is reafforestation?
questions.a: Planting trees again where they had been cut

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is selective cutting?
questions.a: Cutting only the mature trees and leaving the young ones

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is over grazing?
questions.a: Keeping too many animals on the same land so the grass is eaten down to the roots

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any four ways of caring for vegetation.
questions.a: Any four of afforestation, reafforestation, selective cutting, avoiding bush burning, controlling grazing, using energy-saving stoves, gazetting forests, educating people, mulching and crop rotation

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What does it mean to gazette a forest?
questions.a: It means the government marks it off by law as a protected reserve.

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name one type of vegetation found in your own district.
questions.a: (Your own answer — the vegetation really found in your district.)

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give one way you yourself can help care for vegetation.
questions.a: Any correct answer, for example: plant a tree at school or at home and take care of it, or never set fire to the bush.

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is the social environment?
questions.a: People and the things that people make
accepted: People and the things that people make

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is a tribe?
questions.a: A large group of people who share one language, one culture and one origin

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is a clan?
questions.a: A smaller group inside a tribe whose members believe they came from one ancestor

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Which is bigger, a tribe or a clan?
questions.a: A tribe

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is a totem?
questions.a: An animal or plant that a clan respects and does not eat

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is a legend?
questions.a: An old story handed down by word of mouth, telling how a people began

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name the legend told among the Baganda.
questions.a: Kintu and Nambi

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name the legend told in Bugisu.
questions.a: Mundu and Sera

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name the legend told among the Luo-speaking people.
questions.a: Labong and Gipir

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is migration?
questions.a: The movement of people from one place to another to settle

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is the difference between immigration and emigration?
questions.a: Immigration is moving into a place; emigration is moving out of a place.

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any four causes of migration.
questions.a: Any four of search for water, food and pasture; looking for jobs; epidemics; droughts; running away from conflicts; search for fertile soils

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is a drought?
questions.a: A long time without rain

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is a settlement pattern?
questions.a: The way people's homes are arranged in a place

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any five factors that make people settle in a place.
questions.a: Any five of fertile soil, enough and reliable rainfall, trade, jobs, enough food, good security and peace, social services

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any two reasons why some places have very few people.
questions.a: Any two of poor soil, little rain, steep slopes, thick forests, big swamps, insecurity, pests and diseases, no roads or schools or water

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name any six types of work done by people in a district.
questions.a: Any six of fishing, farming, pottery, brick laying, craft working, trading, teaching, office work

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any three problems people face as they do their work.
questions.a: Any three of insecurity and wars, diseases of animals and birds, poor health, poor transport, bad weather, poor prices, lack of money

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Suggest one solution to poor transport.
questions.a: Repair the roads (or use better vehicles, or build bridges)

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name the main tribe found in your own district.
questions.a: (Your own answer — the tribe really found in your district.)

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Who is a leader?
questions.a: A person who guides, plans and organises other people

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any three reasons why we need leaders.
questions.a: Any three of to keep law and order, to plan development, to settle quarrels, to speak for the people, to look after public property, to represent people to government

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name the four groups of leaders found in a district.
questions.a: Political, civic, religious and voluntary leaders
accepted: Political, civic, religious and voluntary leaders

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name the local council levels from the village to the district.
questions.a: LC1 (village), LC2 (parish), LC3 (sub-county), LC4 (county), LC5 (district)

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Who is the head of the local council at the village?
questions.a: The LC1 chairperson

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Who heads the district council?
questions.a: The LC5 chairperson

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Who represents the President in the district?
questions.a: The RDC

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give the full meaning of RDC.
questions.a: Resident District Commissioner

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give the full meaning of CAO.
questions.a: Chief Administrative Officer

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give the full meaning of DISO.
questions.a: District Internal Security Officer

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name any three civic leaders in a district.
questions.a: Any three of CAO, District Health Officer, District Agricultural Officer, magistrate, District Police Commander

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name any four religious leaders.
questions.a: Any four of bishops, priests, reverends, pastors, sheikhs, khadis

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name any two voluntary organisations given in the syllabus.
questions.a: Any two of UWESO, TASO, the Red Cross (Scouts and Guides also accepted)
accepted: the Red Cross (Scouts and Guides also accepted)

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give the four ways in which leaders are chosen.
questions.a: By election, by appointment, through inheritance, and by volunteering

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Which leaders are chosen through inheritance?
questions.a: Cultural leaders — for example a king, a chief or a clan head

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Name the steps followed in an election.
questions.a: Registration, nomination, campaigning, voting, counting, declaring the winner, swearing in

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is a ballot box used for?
questions.a: For putting in the ballot papers during voting

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: What is a secret ballot?
questions.a: Voting in a way that nobody else can see whom you have chosen

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any four qualities of a good leader.
questions.a: Any four of honest, fair, listens to people, keeps promises, hard-working, humble, patient, educated enough

questions.subject: SST
questions.q: Give any three duties of the people towards their leaders.
questions.a: Any three of obey the law, pay taxes, attend meetings, vote wisely, respect leaders, report wrong acts, take part in community work

topics.title: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: What are social services?
questions.a: Things provided to help people live well, which people cannot easily provide alone

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Who has the main responsibility of providing social services?
questions.a: The government

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Name any three groups allowed to provide services on behalf of government.
questions.a: Religious groups, private medical practitioners and business people

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Name any six types of social services.
questions.a: Any six of education, medical, security, transport, water, electricity, housing, road maintenance, banking, postal and communication

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Where is the medical service found?
questions.a: At hospitals, health centres and clinics
accepted: At hospitals, health centres and clinics

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Which service is provided at a police post?
questions.a: Security (law and order)

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Name any six people who provide social services.
questions.a: Any six of teachers, doctors, nurses, veterinary officers, police officers, army officers, drivers, carpenters, bankers, farmers, shopkeepers, local leaders, chiefs, parents

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Who provides education?
questions.a: Teachers

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Who treats animals?
questions.a: A veterinary officer

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: What does a banker do?
questions.a: Keeps people's money safely and lends money

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: What do parents provide for their children?
questions.a: Food, clothing, shelter, school fees, love and care

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Name any five problems met in providing social services.
questions.a: Any five of poverty, bad weather, shortage of food, theft, corruption, irresponsibility, laziness, idleness, high population, poor attitude to work

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: What is corruption?
questions.a: The dishonest use of a position for personal gain — for example taking money meant for services

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Give one solution to poverty.
questions.a: Any one of start income-generating work, join a savings group, work hard, learn a skill, group farming

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Give one solution to theft of school property.
questions.a: Any one of guard the property, fence and lock the buildings, report thieves to the police

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Give one solution to a high population.
questions.a: Any one of family planning and education, building more schools and health centres
accepted: building more schools and health centres

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Give any three ways of caring for a school.
questions.a: Any three of sweep and slash the compound, do not write on the walls, do not break desks, use the latrine properly, plant trees, report damage
accepted: do not write on the walls

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Give any two ways of caring for a borehole.
questions.a: Any two of keep the surroundings clean, repair the handle, do not wash clothes at the source, keep animals away, fence it
accepted: do not wash clothes at the source

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Give the steps to follow when crossing a road safely.
questions.a: Stop · look right · look left · look right again · cross when the road is clear (use a zebra crossing where there is one)

questions.subject: SST
questions.topic: How to Meet People's Needs in Our District
questions.q: Name any two social service centres found in your own district.
questions.a: (Your own answer — two centres really found in your district.)
